purpose: User-centered edge cases where technically correct behavior can still create confusion, distrust, privacy anxiety, or support burden

cases.scenario: User sees a tracking gap after tracker crash
cases.badOutcome: User interprets missing history as personal inactivity or assumes the app is unreliable without explanation.
cases.frictionMitigation: Use neutral wording such as tracking unavailable; link to a concise diagnostic explanation.

cases.scenario: User sees different foreground and visible totals
cases.trigger: Two apps are visible while one is foreground
cases.badOutcome: User assumes one metric is incorrect because totals differ.
cases.frictionMitigation: Explain foreground as active-use metric and visible as window-presence metric at first encounter.

cases.scenario: User manually changes an app category
cases.badOutcome: User thinks only future data changed or worries that raw history was rewritten.
cases.frictionMitigation: Show effective classification and a lightweight explanation that raw observations remain intact.
Present unknown identity as a normal unresolved state with an optional correction action.

cases.scenario: Private browser usage is missing from domain history
cases.badOutcome: User assumes data was lost or browser tracking is inconsistent.
cases.frictionMitigation: Explain once that private browsing intentionally suppresses identifiable browser detail.

cases.badOutcome: Repeated permission prompts become annoying and users disable the entire product.
cases.frictionMitigation: Use a quiet degraded state and one clear route to enable the missing capability later.

cases.scenario: Google sign-in mistaken for sync activation
cases.badOutcome: User believes private usage history was uploaded unexpectedly.
cases.frictionMitigation: Keep signed-in and sync-enabled as separate states in UI and copy.

cases.scenario: Sync is offline for several days
cases.trigger: Laptop remains offline with sync enabled
cases.badOutcome: User thinks the app is malfunctioning because cloud status is stale.
cases.frictionMitigation: Treat sync as secondary health information; local history remains first-class.

cases.scenario: New PC migration finds existing dataset
cases.trigger: User signs in and explicitly enables sync on a new device
cases.badOutcome: User fears duplicate history or accidental merge of unrelated Windows profiles.
cases.frictionMitigation: Preview the dataset/device being joined before merge.

cases.badOutcome: User worries that deletion might affect adjacent dates or another device.
cases.frictionMitigation: Show exact date/time range and whether deletion will propagate.

cases.scenario: System clock changes and timeline appears reordered
cases.badOutcome: User sees apparent duplicate or backward-moving time and assumes corrupted data.
cases.frictionMitigation: Provide a small data-quality marker rather than rewriting history to hide the discontinuity.

cases.badOutcome: User sees odd visual transitions or missing monitor context.
cases.frictionMitigation: Keep monitor metadata secondary and avoid surfacing topology churn unless it explains a discrepancy.

cases.badOutcome: User becomes uncomfortable after seeing sensitive text exposed too prominently.
cases.frictionMitigation: Make title collection visibly independent and allow granular deletion.

cases.badOutcome: User assumes the whole application is heavy or that tracking stopped.
cases.frictionMitigation: Separate UI loading state from tracker state and avoid blocking the shell.

cases.trigger: Same classification changed on two devices
cases.badOutcome: User cannot tell why a label changed and loses confidence in the product.
cases.frictionMitigation: Show which classification is effective and preserve edit history/provenance.

cases.scenario: User opens dashboard immediately after install
cases.badOutcome: Dashboard looks broken or empty without telling user why.
cases.frictionMitigation: Explain that history accumulates in the background and show current tracking status without inventing values.

cases.scenario: No data because user was logged out/locked
cases.trigger: Open historical day containing known system boundary
cases.badOutcome: User interprets absence as zero computer use.
cases.frictionMitigation: Use distinct availability/gap treatment from genuine zero-activity periods.

cases.scenario: Rare adapter failure creates browser detail gap
cases.trigger: Browser extension bridge unavailable for 20 minutes
cases.badOutcome: User thinks all tracking failed because website detail vanished.
cases.frictionMitigation: State exactly which layer was unavailable.
